agent_vs_you: The structure of the agent's plan is the one I would choose: one image-to-video of the user's photo, 6 s, 1:1, sound dropped by the harness. The difference is the prompt. The agent wrote 'preserve the bottle's appearance', which only describes the side the model can SEE. A quarter turn forces minimax to invent the side it cannot see, and an unbranded black bottle invites a printed logo there. That is what happened: white garbled vertical lettering and a round badge rotated into view. The agent did not anticipate that rotation reveals unseen surfaces, and nothing in the catalogue warns about it. It also did not say the cap's carry loop is a rigid part, and the loop bent into an open hook mid-turn. I would state that the bottle is plain matte black on EVERY side with no print anywhere, that the cap and loop are one rigid moulded piece turning with the body, and that the camera is locked off on a tripod. That improves the odds, but the deformation and hallucination are minimax-at-480p behaviour that no prompt fully controls.

your_plan.say: I'll animate your bottle photo into a silent 6-second square clip: the bottle makes a slow quarter turn in place while the camera and table stay perfectly still.

params.prompt_or_change: Locked-off tripod shot, the camera does not move at all. The plain matte black insulated bottle rotates slowly in place on the wooden table, about a quarter turn (90 degrees) to the left over the whole clip, staying upright and centred. The bottle is completely plain matte black on every side: no logo, no text, no label, no badge, no print anywhere on it. The black cap and its carry loop are one rigid moulded piece that turns with the bottle and never bends or changes shape. The table, chair, window, plant and light stay exactly still.

steps.why: This is the catalogue's 'product turning' strength, from the user's own photo, so the bottle is the real one. The prompt fixes the unseen side as plain and the loop as rigid, which are the two things that failed. The harness keeps it square and drops minimax's invented audio, so it is silent.

fix: Add a catalogue line to image-to-video: 'POORLY: turning a product: it paints a logo or text on the side it cannot see and bends thin parts (a loop, a handle, a strap); say the product is plain/unbranded on every side and its parts are rigid, or give an end frame'. Add a planner PROMPTS rule: for any rotation or orbit of a supplied product, describe the hidden side explicitly (same finish, no print) and name the rigid parts. A cheap harness guard: frame at 50% and 100% plus a check ('any text or logo on the product that is not in the source photo?'), retrying once with the negative strengthened when it flags.
evidence: product-bottle.jpg (640x640) shows a completely plain matte black bottle with a black cap and a closed carry loop seen face-on, on a wooden table by a window. bottle-quarter-turn.mp4 is 480x480, 6.58 s, video stream only (silent). A 1 fps strip shows the loop turning (so the rotation did happen), then from about 2 s a white vertical garbled word ('soap'l ele'-like) and a small round badge rotating onto the body. At about 2 s the loop becomes an open hook, and the bottle drifts slightly left. The background is broadly stable with small shifts. The judge's faults (invented branding, morphing loop, slight drift) match what is visible, so the grader is right. 144 credits (6 s at 24/s).
